prompt: Two WebRTC peers are on different private networks with endpoint-dependent NAT mappings. ICE direct host and server-reflexive checks have failed, but a valid TURN relay path succeeds. Which candidate pair can be selected?

options.text: A pair involving a TURN relay candidate
options.explanation: The stated successful relay path supplies connectivity after these direct checks failed. TURN is not guaranteed to work on every network.

options.text: host to host, because it has the highest priority
options.explanation: Priority cannot make a failed path usable; this prompt explicitly says the direct host checks failed.

options.text: srflx to srflx via hole punching
options.explanation: The prompt says those checks failed. Endpoint-dependent mappings can make a STUN-observed address unsuitable for another destination, but NAT labels alone do not prove universal failure.

options.text: No pair; WebRTC cannot work behind symmetric NATs
options.explanation: TURN exists precisely for this case.

workedExample: ICE evaluates actual reachability. In this scenario, direct checks fail and a relay-involving pair succeeds, so the controlling agent can nominate that valid pair. Depending on the selected pair, one or both peers use a TURN allocation. Relay transport must itself be allowed by the network; media traffic consumes relay bandwidth.
